contradicted_texts.text: कु / रु / चु / श्चु / ष्टु: more than one sound → it replaces the WHOLE of the place
contradicted_texts.why: These name one sound of a class (उदित्, 1.1.69) or a class sound-for-sound; each substitute is a single sound.

contradicted_texts.text: विसर्जनीय / अनुस्वार / अनुनासिक / परसवर्ण: more than one sound → it replaces the WHOLE of the place
contradicted_texts.why: Each is the name of a single sound, not a multi-sound substitute.

contradicted_texts.text: बहुवचन / द्विवचन / तृतीया / नपुंसकम् / तुल्यम् / एक-शेष / लोपः: more than one sound → it replaces the WHOLE of the place
contradicted_texts.why: Not substitutes (number/case/gender/atideśa rules) or not sounds (लोप); 1.1.55 is outside its scope.

contradicted_texts.text: मुम् / ईट् / अम्: more than one sound → it replaces the WHOLE of the place
contradicted_texts.why: Augments: placed by 1.1.46/1.1.47, they replace nothing.

contradicted_texts.text: णल्: a single sound → it replaces the LAST sound
contradicted_texts.why: णल् is anekāl when taught (its ण् is not yet an it) and replaces the whole (Padamañjarī 3.4.82: “णकारस्यानेकालत्वात्सर्वादेशः”).

1.1.55.proposed_gloss: a substitute of more than one sound (not counting it-letters), or a śit one, replaces the WHOLE item
1.1.55.proposed_explanation: A substitute of more than one real sound, or one marked श्, replaces the whole 6th-case item (अस्तेर्भूः). Count without it-letters: उत्, अङ्, सिच्, कु, रु are one sound (→ 1.1.52); डा and णल् count their first letter. Augments and case/number rules are outside it. (Bhāṣya: “नानुबन्धकृतमनेकाल्त्वं भवतीति”)

gaps.condition: Only a real substitute counts: an augment, a newly introduced suffix, a nipātana, a prakṛtibhāva, a number/gender/case rule or an atideśa introduces nothing to be sthānivat.

1.1.56.proposed_gloss: a substitute keeps the original's status (dhātu, aṅga, sup, tiṅ …) — but not for a rule that depends on a sound of the original
1.1.56.proposed_explanation: A substitute counts as the original for later rules that depend on its status (dhātu, aṅga, kṛt, sup, tiṅ, pada), not for a rule that depends on one of its sounds (द्यौः, पन्थाः). 1.1.61.proposed_explanation: लुक्, श्लु and लुप् name the disappearance of a suffix. A rule ordering one of them removes the whole suffix, not just its last sound, and the name matters later (1.1.63: after a लु-elision the aṅga undergoes no operation caused by that suffix). 1.1.62.proposed_explanation: When a suffix has been elided by लोप, the operations it would cause still take place, as if it were present. 1.1.63 limits this: if the elision is by a word containing लु (लुक्, श्लु, लुप्), the aṅga undergoes no operation caused by it. (Kāśikā: “प्रत्ययलोपे कृते प्रत्ययलक्षणं प्रत्ययहेतुकं कार्यं भवति।”)

1.1.65.proposed_explanation: उपधा names the single sound just before the final sound of a word or root — one sound only, never a group. A rule on the उपधा changes that sound, not the last one (शास् → शिष्टः: the आ becomes इ). (Kaumudī: “अन्त्यादलः पूर्वो वर्ण उपधासंज्ञः स्यात्”)

PIS 18.proposed_gloss: sometimes only PART of an earlier word runs on (e.g. पद from पदान्तात्)
PIS 18.proposed_explanation: Occasionally only part of a word in an earlier sūtra continues by anuvṛtti, not the whole word: at 6.1.131 only पद of पदान्तात् (6.1.109) runs on. The commentators say where this happens. (Śekhara: “क्वचिदेकदेशोऽप्यनुवर्तते”)

gaps.condition: Not in saṃjñā rules (PIS 27; jñāpaka सुप्तिङन्तम्) — where commentators still read tadanta (1.1.23, 1.1.38, 1.2.46) they justify it by sāmarthya or अर्थवत्.
gaps.why: Not taught; the generic card is printed at 1.1.23 (and the step at 1.1.25) crediting PIS 23 in saṃjñā rules.

gaps.condition: When the suffix is the condition (a 7th, ‘when X follows’), only the tadādi part applies.
A suffix must be NAMED as a known element: not one being prescribed or changed (luk, ādeśa, its own accent), not part of a nipātana, not a homonym.
In the uttarapada heading a suffix means only itself (PIS 25).
Only where suffixes alone are named (not a term covering suffix and non-suffix).
Definition: a named suffix = the word from its base up to the suffix.
PIS 24, 26, 28; anarthaka अन्/इन्/अस्/मन् go under 1.1.72.

contradicted_texts.text: a suffix named in a rule stands for the word that ENDS in that suffix (starting from what it was added to)
contradicted_texts.why: Result right, reason contradicted: in a saṃjñā rule PIS 23 does not apply (Śekhara PIS 27: “संज्ञाविधौ प्रत्ययग्रहणे तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”); the tadanta there rests on sāmarthya.

PIS 23.proposed_gloss: a suffix named stands for the word from its base up to that suffix — not in saṃjñā rules, nor for the suffix being taught
PIS 23.proposed_explanation: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

gaps.condition: Where a kṛt suffix is named (in general or a particular one), the kṛdanta with a gati or kāraka before it is meant too.
Jñāpaka: अनन्तरः in 6.2.49, where it is set aside.

PIS 28.proposed_gloss: a kṛt suffix named also covers the kṛdanta with a gati or kāraka before it
PIS 28.proposed_explanation: Where a rule names a kṛt suffix — kṛt in general or a particular one — the word with a gati or kāraka before the kṛdanta is meant too. Pāṇini's अनन्तरः in 6.2.49 shows the maxim exists, and there it is set aside. (Śekhara: “कृद्ग्रहणे गतिकारकपूर्वस्यापि ग्रहणम्”)

gaps.condition: Scope: the sarūpa test of 3.1.94 — it only ever DENIES dissimilarity; it says nothing where suffixes differ in real sounds, and needs a real utsarga–apavāda pair in the dhātu section.
gaps.why: Gloss says markers do not make suffixes dissimilar, but not that this is for 3.1.94; no explanation.

gaps.why: The 3.1.99 card says 'markers removed before comparing'; the outcome (no option) is not said.

gaps.condition: PIS 6/7 share the opening नानुबन्धकृतम्… but are different maxims.

contradicted_texts.text: श is an apavāda of तव्यत्, तव्य, अनीयर् (3.1.96; all dhātus) → श (अ) ≠ तव्यत् … → they stay available as options
contradicted_texts.why: The audit correction is appended but the wrong claim is still shown: Kāśikā names ण as the utsarga (“णस्यापवादः”), sarūpa with श once markers go — which is why 3.1.139 needs its own विभाषा (Śekhara PIS 8).

PIS 8.proposed_gloss: in the sarūpa test of 3.1.94, marker letters are ignored: suffixes differing only in markers count as the same form
PIS 8.proposed_explanation: For 3.1.94 (an exception of different form blocks only optionally), suffixes are compared without their it-letters: अण्/क, यत्/ण्यत्, घञ्/अच्/अप् count as the same form, so such an exception blocks the general suffix outright. It never makes suffixes with different real sounds alike. (Śekhara: “नानुबन्धकृतमसारूप्यम्”)
